questions.question: Which of the following was the first site where Indus Valley Civilization was discovered?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harappa**__.

 
• **Harappa**:

 
 
• Harappan culture planned its towns with their chessboard system, streets, drainage pipes, and chess pits.
 
• Rectangular houses with brick-line bathrooms and wells together with their stairways are found in all Harappan sites.
 
• Harappans have well connected central drainage system.
 
• Harappa is known as the city of granaries.
 
• **The civilization was first identified in 1921 at Harappa (Punjab) and then in 1922 at Mohenjodaro (Sindh, Pakistan)**.
 
 
 
• Major findings in Kot Diji (Pakistan) of Harappan site are a tar, statues of bull and mother goddess.
 
• 
 
Major findings of Mohenjodaro are the Great bath, Great granary, Assembly hall, Steatite image of bearded man, and Seal of Pashupati.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is true about the religious practices of the Harappan people?

options.text: They had a class of priests

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**No temple has been unearthed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The people of this civilization had a **rich culture and complex social and religious systems**.
 
• However, much about their religious beliefs and practices remains a **mystery due to the lack of decipherable written records**.
 
• Archaeological evidence suggests that the **Harappans may have worshipped a variety of deities, as indicated by the numerous figurines and seals discovered at various site**s. These include depictions of what appear to be goddess figures, often referred to as the "**Mother Goddess**," and a figure in a yogic posture, often referred to as "**Pashupati" or "proto-Shiva**."
 
• Despite these findings,** no specific structures identifiable as temples have been unearthed in any of the major Harappan sites**. This suggests that formal places of worship, as we understand them today, may not have been a part of Harappan religious practice.
 
• It's possible that **religious rituals were conducted in homes or in public spaces, or that certain buildings** served multiple purposes, including religious functions. However, without definitive evidence, these remain theories.
 
• Therefore, based on current archaeological findings and historical records, it is accurate to say that no temple has been unearthed from the Harappan civilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **About Indus valley Civilization**

 
• **Script and Language**: The Harappan script is yet to be deciphered. Over 400 distinct Indus symbols have been found on seals, small tablets, ceramic pots and more than a dozen other materials. Despite many attempts, the 'script' has not yet been deciphered and hence, much of Harappan life remains a mystery.
 
• **Art and Craft**: The Harappans were skilled craftsmen. They made beautiful pottery, seals, beads, and ornaments. The pottery was often decorated with geometric and animal designs. The seals, usually made of steatite, depicted a variety of animals and mythical beings and were likely used for trade.
 
• **Trade and Commerce**: The Harappans engaged in trade with their neighbors in the Persian Gulf and Mesopotamia. Many Indus seals and a piece of Indus pottery have been discovered at ancient city sites in Mesopotamia.
 
• **Decline of the Civilization**: The reasons for the decline of the Indus Valley Civilization are not clear. It's believed that a combination of factors including climate change, tectonic events, or a change in river patterns could have contributed to its decline. There's also a theory about an Aryan invasion, but it's a subject of ongoing debate among scholars.
 
• **Rediscovery**: The ruins of the Indus Valley Civilization were first discovered in the 1920s by a railway engineer named R. D. Banerji. Two of the main sites, Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro, have since been extensively excavated.
 
• **Legacy**: The civilization's sophisticated urban planning, architecture, and drainage systems indicate a highly organized society. Some of its practices, such as the cultivation of cotton and rice, have had a lasting impact and continue to be important in the region.

questions.question: Which among the following period of the stone age **first** witnessed the domestication of animals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Mesolithic Age__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mesolithic Age falls roughly from **9000 B.C. to 4000 B.C**.
 
• It was the transitional phase between the Paleolithic Age and Neolithic Age.
 
• Although Mesolithic men were still dependent largely on hunting, now they used began **taming the animals** like dog, sheep, goat, cow-ox, buffalo, wild horse, etc.
 
• The earliest evidence of the taming of animals was found from **Adamgarh of Madhya Pradesh** and **Baghore of Rajasthan**. They are Mesolithic sites. **Hence, Option 4 is correct**.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Paleolithic: 

 
 
• It is the earliest Stone age period dating 2.6 million years ago.
 
• The age is distinguished by most primitive stone tools. Humans during the era grouped together in small “bands” and were involved in gathering plants, fishing, and hunting.
 
• The paleolithic period is the longest in human history.
 
• The age can be divided into lower Paleolithic, Middle Paleolithic, and Upper Paleolithic. 
 
• During the end of the age, people developed spiritual and religious beliefs as depicted in some of the excavations.
 
 
 
• Mesolithic: It is the second period of the stone age between Paleolithic and Neolithic. The start and end of the age vary by geographical region. It is a transition period from hunting and gathering as in Paleolithic to domestication as in Neolithic. The tools used were the mode V chipped stone tools (microliths).
 
• Neolithic: It is the 3rd period of the stone age and is often referred to as the “New stone age”. Its time period is considered to be around 10,200 BC to 4,500BC, which ended with the beginning of the “Bronze Age”.
 
• **Microlith**: It is a small tool made up of flint or chert, used to form the points of hunting weapons.

questions.question: Which of the following is also known as ‘New Stone Age’ in the civilisation history of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neolithic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Neolithic period **is the **final division **of the **Stone Age**, with a **wide-ranging set **of **developments **that **appear **to **have arisen independently **in **several parts **of **the world**.
 
• **The new stone age **is also called **Neolithic**.
 
• The **Neolithic period **is significant for its **megalithic architecture**, **the spread of agricultural practices**, and the **use of polished stone tools**.
 
• The **Neolithic Revolution **started around **10,000 B.C. **in the **Fertile Crescent**, a **boomerang-shaped region **of the **Middle East **where humans first took up **farming**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In archaeology, the **Epipalaeolithic **or **Epipaleolithic **is a term for a **period occurring **between the **Upper Paleolithic **and **Neolithic during **the **Stone Age**.
 
• During the **Mesolithic period **(about **10,000 B.C. to 8,000 B.C.), **humans used **small stone tools**, now also **polished and sometimes crafted **with **points **and **attached to antlers**, **bone**, or **wood to serve **as **spears and arrows**. 
 
• The **Paleolithic Period**, or **Old Stone Age**, **Ancient technological **or **cultural stage **characterized by the **use of rudimentary chipped stone tools**. During the **Lower Paleolithic **(c**. 2,500,000–200,000 years ago**), simple pebble tools and **crude stone choppers **were made by the **earliest humans**.

questions.question: Punch-marked coins from the sixth century BCE onwards were made of silver and which of the following metals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Punch-marked coins are made up of **silver and copper**.
 
• They are also known as **Aahat coins**.
 
• They are classified into two groups **local and universal**.
 
 
• Local punched marked coins carry **one to four symbols** depending upon their location and size.
 
• Universal punched marked coins carry **five symbols** and are mainly issued by **Magadh Dynasty**.
 
 
 
• The coins were 1st introduced by **Janapadas and Mahajanapadas of the Indo-Gangetic Plain**.
 
• They are created by **hammering **with the help of **punches and dies**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: "Banawali"-a major city of Indus Valley Civilization is presently located at which among the following states of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Haryana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** **Banawali is the major city of the Indus Valley civilization which is located in present-day Haryana state in India.**

__
 
• **Banawali:**

 
 
• Banawali site was excavated by **R.S.Bist in 1973 **in Fatehabad, Haryana.
 
• The Replica of the plough was from a field found in the Banawali district.
 
• The **clay figure of the mother goddess** was also found there.
 
 
 
• **Lothal Site:**
 
 
• Lothal was excavated by **S.R.Rao in 1954** in Gujarat.
 
• It was a port city as evidence shows.
 
• The evidence of the dockyard was found at Lothal.
 
 
 
• **Dholavira Site:**
 
 
• It was excavated by **J.P.Joshi in 1967 **near the Kutchh area of Gujarat.
 
• **A unique water harnessing system** was founded at the Dholavira site.
 
• Dholavira has yielded the longest inscription comprising ten large-sized signs of the Harappan script.
 
• It was embedded on a three-meter-long board.
 
 
 
• **Kalibangan:**
 
 
• Kalibangan means the **bangles of black colour**.
 
• It was first excavated by **Amalanand Ghosh in 1951 and later B.V.Lal and B.K. Thapar in 1961**.
 
• It was excavated in Hanumangarh, Rajasthan.
 
• The evidence of a **ploughed field** was found here the first time.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** The Indus Valley Civilization:**

 
 
• It was a civilization that was mostly founded in the Indus River Valley.
 
• The time period of the Indus Valley Civilization was from **2600 BC to 1900 BC**.
 
• The term Indus valley civilization was coined by **John Marshall.**
 
• This civilization was spread over Sindh, Baluchistan, Haryana, Rajasthan, Punjab, Western Uttar Pradesh, and Northern Maharashtra.
 
• The important sites of the Indus Valley Civilization were **Harappa, Mohenjodaro, Chanhudaro, Lothal, Kalibanga, Banawali, Dholavira, Rangpur,** etc.

questions.question: Which of the following animals has been found engraved on most of the seals of Indus Valley Civilization?
questions.solution:
Indus Valley Civilization

__
 
• **Indus Valley Civilization** was one of those early urban civilizations that were originated in 2300 BC and were developed in the river basins of Sutlej, Ravi, and Indus.
 
• Indus Valley Civilization peoples cultivate many crops such as Barley, Wheat, Melon seeds, and oil crops like Sesame, Mustard, and Dates. These were traded by farmers with other people. 
 
• The most typical Indus seal is square, with a set of symbols along the top, an animal in the centre, and one or more symbols at the bottom. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

**Seals**

__
 
• **The unicorn is the most common motif on Indus seals **and appears to represent a mythical animal that Greek and Roman sources trace back to the Indian subcontinent. A relatively long inscription of eight symbols runs along the top of the seal. ***Hence option 3 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Archaeologists have discovered thousands of seals, mostly made of steatite, and occasionally of agate, chert, copper, faience and terracotta, with beautiful figures of animals, such as** unicorn bull**, rhinoceros, tiger, elephant, bison, goat, buffalo, etc.
 
• The realistic rendering of these animals in various moods is remarkable. The purpose of producing seals was mainly commercial.
 
• It appears that the seals were also used as amulets, carried on the persons of their owners, perhaps as modern-day identity cards. The standard Harappan seal was a square plaque 2×2 square inches, made from steatite.
 
• Every seal is engraved in a pictographic script which is yet to be deciphered. Some seals have also been found in ivory.
 
• They all bear a great variety of motifs, **most often of animals including those of the bull, with or without the hump, the elephant, tiger, goat and also monsters.**
